checks.notes: Finding concerns protocol logic inconsistency, not token standards
Attack path involves normal admin behavior, not user error

Admin pausing a token is EXPECTED behavior per project docs ('Pause tokens for black swan events'). The bug is the disproportionate protocol response (global DoS) to correct admin action. This is a logic inconsistency between claim() and calculateClaimAmount(), not an admin acting recklessly.
Root cause is in StableYieldAccumulator.sol lines 434 and 576, which are in scope

Checked against all 8 known issues. 'Owner trust' and 'Pauser trust' known issues cover centralization risk of trusted roles acting maliciously. This finding is about a code logic bug causing unintended side effects when the admin acts correctly and as intended.
Finding demonstrates concrete code inconsistency with exact line references verified in source
calculateClaimAmount() is actively used by callers and ClaimArbitrage to determine claim viability; its inconsistency amplifies the DoS impact

sourceVerification.claimLine434: if (tokenConfigs[token].paused) revert TokenIsPaused(); -- CONFIRMED in source

validityCheck.notes: VALID finding. The code inconsistency between claim() (line 434, reverts on paused token) and calculateClaimAmount() (line 576, skips paused token) is verified in source. This is a genuine logic bug, not an admin trust issue. The admin is performing the intended action of pausing a single token during a depeg event, but the code causes a disproportionate global DoS on all yield claiming. Does not overlap with any of the 8 known issues.
